title: Dependency and Action Supply-Chain Security knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Dependency and Action Supply-Chain Security?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Supply-chain safety includes reviewing third-party actions, pinning them to full commit SHAs, tracking dependencies, and monitoring security updates.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Supply-chain safety includes reviewing third-party actions, pinning them to full commit SHAs, tracking dependencies, and monitoring security updates.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of dependency and action supply-chain security: Supply-chain safety includes reviewing third-party actions, pinning them to full commit SHAs, tracking dependencies, and monitoring security updates. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Reviewing third-party action source code”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
questions.explanation: Reviewing third-party action source code: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to dependency and action supply-chain security?
options: Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Supply-chain safety includes reviewing third-party actions, pinning them to full commit SHAs, tracking dependencies, and monitoring security updates. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
